items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: he had been in ... Bob Crosby

ctx.x: Was there a strong sense of competition between the big bands at that time?

Yes there was. And stealing musicians from each other was very big. When I started listening to music, they were set — I mean Ellington’s band was Ellington’s band and somebody else was something else. But I don’t know when the stealing of musicians and trading and moving around, but good night, just while I was married to Shorty, he moved around to a number of bands. He had been in, when I came into his life he had been in Jimmy Dorsey’s — well he’d been in Ben Pollack’s band, and Jimmy Dorsey, and Bob Crosby,…

and he got a car like him, and the payments I think were like $85 a month, and he was only making $85 a week. It was pretty dicey. And he was standing next to his car in this costume, and Bobby Burnett came by. He was a trumpet player with Charlie Barnet. And he said, “Shorty, what happened?” Shorty said, “man when I change I change all the way.” So here he was playing like Roy.
